scope: C11 arm B (Semantic Director 1.0), all 40 benchmark beats; one PRIMARY category per beat, from the frozen key, the B contract, the blind description, both judge passes and (for B05 B09 B13 B17 B19 B21 B27 B29 B31 B40) the strip itself. Exploratory analysis of a finished NO SHIP experiment — it does not re-score or re-decide C11.

A_textOnly.meaning: B chose a quote card; no picture carried meaning (ADDS 0), the viewer restated the text
A_textOnly.note: B07 lost 100 -> 50 (A's picture of the thermostat loop beat the bare sentence); the three that worked are beats whose whole point IS the sentence (a caveat, a slogan, a placement claim)

B_claimLogic.meaning: the shown claim has the wrong polarity / attribution / scope: a rejected premise, a counterfactual expectation, one half of a contrast, a hedged argument shown flat, a negated condition shown positive, a concessive dropped

beats.B05: rejected premise quoted as the claim ('I hear your point about her intellect being useless…' — the speaker pushes back next) -> viewer: conceding; WRONG
beats.B09: counterfactual expectation shown as fact ('trained that doing nothing equals safety … they should just fuse to the floor. But when…'); card over the source scene's classroom -> 'school'; WRONG
beats.B10: only the setup half of a temporary-vs-permanent contrast quoted ('They give you an action item')
beats.B39: a hedged legal argument ('That's self-defense … Maybe you argue heat of the moment') shown as a flat verdict; the second, debatable strike lost
beats.B16: negated condition ('If you DON'T kick things around … you lose your bearing') drawn as the person draining the stock — the absence is the cause
beats.B04: rejected motive ('not because you want to paint') omitted; only the true motive shown — the contrast that is the point is gone
beats.B20: concessive lost ('they end up laughing EVEN THOUGH the events are harrowing') — drawn as mom's mood passing to the kids

C_wrongRepresentation.meaning: the claim was right but the chosen picture says something else

beats.B17: 'widen the map' drawn as a stock FILLING -> 'values fill the map'; a widening needs a size change, not a level
beats.B27: 'pave over a crater with capital' drawn as a full CRATER tank DRAINING when capital acts — inverted; the hole should stay while money covers it
beats.B32: the label 'grace' on a person read as a character named Grace
beats.B36: the decisive link (truth -> demands action -> action means death) not drawn; blinders read as blocking the truth
beats.B35: environment beat: an unnamed second person and a generic meeting icon lost A's specific setting

D_framingScaleTiming.meaning: the right change, too small / unmarked to read

beats.B21: a row of ten tiny figures on a large empty board, the cause ring on the group itself, the cause (winning at people's expense) not drawn; still +33 pp

E_inventedCausality.meaning: the picture asserts a causal link the narration does not

beats.B26: a discovery ('Graham … realized that this company held a portfolio') drawn as Graham making the portfolio appear -> 'Graham shaped it' = the key's listed wrong inference 'Graham invented the bonds'

F_successfulMechanism.meaning: staged state change read as the narration's mechanism / comparison / result

beats.B13: traffic patterns -> the listener's face turns: 16.7 -> 83.3
beats.B29: same notes, two lanes on one scale (Jack low / August high): 50 -> 100
beats.B31: helplessness carried from room 1 to room 2, the person resigned: 50 -> 100

G_stagedNoGain.meaning: staged (action / environment) but no change in score

totals: A 14 (11 flat/worse + 3 worked) · B 7 · C 5 · D 1 · E 1 · F 9 · G 3 = 40
lessonsForC12: Claim logic is the biggest fixable cause of harm: 7 beats; 2 of B's WRONG beats (B05, B09) are polarity errors. The narration's own structure (but / even though / if … don't / maybe / I hear your point) decides what the screen may assert.
Text-only is not the problem per se (3 worked); quoting the WRONG sentence is. A quote must be the asserted claim, on a neutral ground, never a rejected premise / counterfactual / setup half.
Representation must match the claim's verb: widen = size, cover = layer over a hole that stays, discover = reveal (present: false -> true without a causal token), not create.
Labels must not look like proper names unless they are cast members (B32).
The successful pattern (F) is narrow and consistent: one cause, one entity whose state visibly changes, the after state held; comparisons on one scale.
